Its Li-rich, Al3+ cation is weakly reducible and only mildly Lewis-acidic, so it should be less prone to displacing La or Zr from LLZO than the zirconate, silicate and phosphate coatings. Fluoride anions also avoid the oxidation risk of chlorides at 4 V.

proposals.hypothesis: Li2MgSiO4 is a Li-rich orthosilicate with a divalent Mg2+ cation, expected to be a wide-gap insulator and oxidatively stable at 4 V vs Li. Mg2+ is a weak Lewis acid and is not easily reduced, so it should be less prone than Zr4+ or P5+ to displacing La from LLZO. Earlier silicate and phosphate coatings formed La-containing products, so a Mg-silicate with a different cation mix tests whether the contact penalty can drop below the 0.05 eV threshold.

It is also oxidatively stable at 4 V vs Li, so it may give a lower interface penalty than Li3PO4.
